cells.tense: Right now you're the one moving what matters into other people's hands.
cells.ask: Take one piece you care about and put it in front of one person this week. When they push back, stay in it long enough to find where your telling and their understanding meet.
cells.core:
There's something you carry, and you move it by feeling before volume. Bring you near what connects a room and the room changes shape under you. What you hand over arrives already formed by care, and that's why it stays longer than it should.

You can tell what's still alive in what you pass on from what's gone stiff, and you do that without a speech about it. Whoever's across from you keeps your attention even while you're teaching them something. One caution, small and real: leave a piece untouched too long and the contact goes quiet. Pushback belongs to the exchange, and it's not a crack in it.
cells.sheetLine: You move what matters, and you move it by feeling.
cells.verb: Carrying what matters to you into other people's hands
cells.place: Where the pull you steer by is recognized, not given

cells.tense: You're reaching toward a version of this that hasn't arrived yet, and acting like it already has.
cells.ask: Before you set the next thing in motion, take one piece you keep staging ahead of time and put it where it actually lives — written down, played out, said once to a person who's here.
cells.core:
Somewhere ahead there's a room that isn't built, and you're already furnishing it. You've mapped what they'll need before they've said a word, and the meaning you're carrying is real — you can see how it would land, how it would travel, how it would hold. When you're on solid footing you read the actual person in front of you and let that shift the message.

Instead you're spending on the version that hasn't arrived. Answering before the question. Staging connection rather than making it. The intensity is still the point, but it's landed on an audience that isn't in the building.
cells.sheetLine: You're furnishing a room that isn't built yet.
cells.verb: Carrying what matters to you into other people's hands
cells.place: Where the pull you steer by is recognized, not given

cells.tense: A door you already passed through is standing open behind you, and you're still facing it.
cells.ask: Pick the piece that matters most and work it out on paper alone first — a page only you'll read, tracing how it would move. Then decide whether it's worth taking out loud.
cells.core:
You carry something and you don't bring it out. It sits there, familiar and unoffered, and the offering is what stopped. What you understand hasn't gone anywhere, and neither have you — you're just not bringing it to the table.

At your best you turn this into something that could travel with someone else. A private page can do that — the pattern gets solid when you trace it with no one interrupting, and solidity is what a person can pick up. You don't have to feel your way to the door. Write it down, see the shape of it, and the urge to share can come back on its own after that.
cells.sheetLine: You have something to pass on, and you've stopped passing it on.

cells.tense: The pen is moving across the page while you talk as if someone else were holding it.
cells.ask: Name the one thing you brought back that you've been calling 'just something I picked up' — out loud, once — and decide by your own judgment whether it's worth keeping.
cells.core:
You're already moving what people around you come to believe, in what you repeat and what you let sit. But you describe it as the room's, the text's, the tradition's — as if the meaning did its own thing and you happened to be nearby. On solid footing you'd call the work yours without it being a claim about you, and the deciding about what to keep would stay in your hands.

The moving is already running. The credit for it isn't. Either way, the deciding is yours to own — and it belongs to the work, not to your worth.
cells.sheetLine: The moving is already yours. You call it the room's.
